The codec the PC compresses the video with. If the PC or this device doesn\'t support the one you pick, another one is used.

string-array.name: apollo_info_video_format_texts
string-array.item: The best one both the PC and this device support (recommended)
The most efficient: the same quality with less data. Needs a recent GPU
More efficient than H.264, supported almost everywhere
The most compatible, but needs more bitrate for the same quality
Very low latency, only on a fast local network (200 Mbps or more). Experimental

resources.string: Streams in HDR (or 10-bit SDR) when the game and the PC\'s graphics card support it. Needs a GPU that can encode HEVC Main 10.
Stretches the picture to fill the whole screen, even when the aspect ratios don\'t match. When off, black bars fill the rest.

Only with PyroWave and \"Sync to host frame timing\". When a frame arrives late or loses packets, it\'s shown with what has arrived, a little blurred, instead of being skipped. Cutting more means fewer stutters on a busy network, but more blur. With Vibepollo and other Vibeshine-based hosts it\'s always Off: they can\'t show a frame that\'s missing data.

string-array.name: apollo_info_pyrowave_late_frames_texts
string-array.item: Late frames are shown late, always sharp
Cuts few frames, blur is rare
Cuts more frames: fewer stutters, more blur
Shows almost anything: the fewest stutters, the most blur

resources.string: How the video gets to the screen.

string-array.name: apollo_info_video_renderer_texts
string-array.item: The decoder draws straight to the screen: the simplest and most proven
Adds dithering and its own, more even frame pacing. Experimental

resources.string: Adds very fine moving noise that hides the color banding in gradients, most visible in HDR. Vulkan renderer only.
Uses the full range of colors instead of the reduced one of video. If your screen doesn\'t handle it properly, detail is lost in very light and very dark areas.
Also lists the highest frame rates, like 90, 120 or 144 FPS. They can lower latency on high-end devices, but cause stutter and instability on devices that can\'t keep up.
Lets the screen drop to the frame rate of the stream instead of staying at its highest refresh rate. Saves battery, for a little more latency.

Leave at 0 to measure the real refresh rate of the screen when the stream starts and ask the PC for a frame rate that lines up with it (143.65 FPS on a 143.65 Hz panel). Enter a rate to send that one instead. Experimental.
How frames are shown as they arrive: how much latency and smoothness count.

string-array.name: apollo_info_frame_pacing_texts
string-array.item: Shows the latest frame right away: the least latency, but it can stutter
Lines frames up with the screen and skips the extra ones
Like Balanced, but asks the PC for 1 FPS less than the screen, so frames never pile up
Never skips a frame: the smoothest, but latency can grow a lot
Shows frames at the pace the PC made them, with a small margin set by the jitter buffer. Best with Vulkan

resources.string: Only with \"Sync to host frame timing\". Adds a small delay to absorb network hiccups, so every frame arrives in time to be shown: more delay, fewer stutters.

string-array.name: apollo_info_jitter_buffer_texts
string-array.item: The least delay, but a few frames may show unevenly
The middle ground between latency and smoothness (recommended)
The smoothest, with about 10 ms more delay

resources.string: Turns on extra decoder options that can lower latency on Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, 8 Gen 3 and 8 Elite, Exynos and MediaTek chips. Experimental: if the video misbehaves, turn it off.
Hides the warnings that show during the stream when the connection is slow or unstable.
Lets the system audio effects (equalizers, Dolby and the like) work during the stream, but can add audio latency.
Plays the audio both on the PC and on this device.
How far a stick has to move before the movement counts, so a worn stick doesn\'t move things by itself. Some games use a larger deadzone anyway.
Each connected controller is a different player on the PC. When off, all controllers act as one, and the PC always sees a controller, even with none connected.
When the stream starts, the controllers you have connected join the PC right away. Otherwise the PC only connects each one at its first button press.
Connect the controllers to the PC when the stream starts, without pressing a button
Swaps A with B and X with Y, on controllers and on the on-screen controls. Handy with Nintendo-style controllers.
The controller\'s touchpad (like the DualSense one) moves the PC\'s mouse, even when the PC sees a controller with a touchpad.
Lets the PC ask for gyroscope data when the controller has it. When off, it saves a little battery and network if the game doesn\'t use it.
If the controller has no gyroscope, or your Android version doesn\'t support it, this device\'s own is used. Note: the PC may then see the controller as a PlayStation one.
When the controller acts as a mouse, the chosen stick scrolls pages.
If the controller can\'t vibrate, this device vibrates in its place.
Uses a built-in USB driver for Xbox controllers on devices that don\'t support them by themselves.
Uses the built-in USB driver for all supported controllers, even when Android already supports them. Try it if an Xbox controller doesn\'t work properly.
What touching the screen does during the stream.

string-array.name: apollo_info_touch_mode_texts
string-array.item: Touches reach the PC as on a touch screen, several fingers at once
Tap where you want to click: the cursor jumps there
The screen is a touchpad: drag to move the cursor, tap to click

resources.string: Recognizes 3, 4 and 5 finger taps in multi-touch mode. Turn it off if an app on the PC needs those touches itself. In the other modes the gestures always work.
Sends the Back and Forward mouse buttons to the PC. On some devices it can stop right click from working.
The cursor goes exactly where you point, as in a remote desktop, so mouse acceleration feels more natural. It doesn\'t work with many games.
Touch the left edge of the screen during the stream to show the brightness slider. Those touches don\'t reach the PC.
Hides all the on-screen buttons except L3 and R3.
Long press Ctrl, Shift, Alt or Win to keep it held down until you tap it again. Handy for shortcuts like Ctrl+C.
The controller button to hold during the stream to open the game menu.
Keyboard shortcuts of your own (like Alt+Tab or Win+D) to send to the PC from the game menu.
If a stream is running when the device goes to sleep, it resumes by itself when it wakes up.
What happens to the stream when you switch to another app or go to the home screen. The game stays open on the PC in every case.

string-array.name: apollo_info_leave_app_texts
string-array.item: The connection ends: to go back, start the game again from the list
The connection ends and starts again by itself when you come back, in a few seconds. Nothing is used in the meantime

The connection stays open with the video paused, so the picture is back right away. The PC keeps streaming, which uses battery and network. If the connection drops meanwhile, it reconnects when you come back
The stream stays visible in a small window over the other apps. You can watch it but not control it, and closing the window closes the stream

resources.string: While the stream runs in the background, you keep hearing it: a game, music or a call on the PC.
Lets GeForce Experience change the game\'s settings to suit the stream.
Hides the Android bars in the app. Swipe from the edge of the screen to bring them back.
Smaller covers in the games grid, so more of them fit on screen.
How long to hold the buttons above before their shortcut runs. A shorter press reaches the game as usual.
Hold Select and press the bumper. Neither button reaches the game.
The stats go back to their defaults: style, positions, values and their order, opacity and colors.
